Severe Floods Disrupt Bangladesh Automotive Supply Chains

Severe monsoon floods have inundated key automotive manufacturing zones and transport corridors in Bangladesh, causing significant disruption to the industry’s supply chains. Heavy rains over the past week have left several assembly plants and component factories in the Narayanganj and Gazipur districts under water, while critical highways and rail links to the Port of Chattogram are reported to be impassable.

Industry sources estimate that as of Thursday, at least six major automotive plants have suspended operations, either due to direct flooding or a lack of parts deliveries. The Bangladesh Automotive Manufacturers Association (BAMA) stated that ongoing assessments indicate production losses could exceed 3,000 units per day if the situation persists. “Our priority is the safety of our workforce, but it is clear the disruption to output and shipments is already substantial,” said BAMA president Anwar Rahman.

Logistics bottlenecks are also mounting as floodwaters block routes used to import raw materials and export finished vehicles. “Both inbound and outbound transport have been severely affected. We are facing delays of up to a week for essential components such as wiring harnesses and suspension parts,” said Shamsul Haque, supply chain director at Eastern Motors Ltd. Haque noted that some suppliers had already shifted to air freight at considerable extra cost.

Analysts warn that prolonged flooding could strain the industry’s recovery from recent pandemic-era slowdowns. “The automotive sector is highly dependent on just-in-time deliveries, so even short disruptions can cascade through the system,” observed Meherun Akter, an industry analyst at South Asia Economics.

With water levels still rising in some areas and heavy rain forecast to continue, the full extent of the impact remains uncertain. Local union representatives have called for urgent government support to safeguard jobs and stabilize critical infrastructure as the emergency continues.
